title: Closeout, quality evidence and follow-up
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Electrical licences and credentials (last updated 23 June 2026); NSW Government, Plumbing, draining and gasfitting (last updated 31 July 2026).
audience: Property manager partner workers who close out jobs and manage follow-up
learningOutcomes: Record before and after evidence that shows what changed and what did not.
Mark the source of a problem as resolved only with evidence.
Schedule follow-up monitoring and propose the follow-up work for approval.

instruction.heading: Evidence before and after
instruction.body: Closeout starts with evidence. Take before and after photographs from the same position, with consent, so the change can be compared. Record the measurements, the materials used and the condition when the work ended. A clean appearance is not proof that the cause has been fixed. A patch can look finished while the moisture behind it is still active, and a closeout must say so where that is the case.

instruction.heading: Record what is unresolved
instruction.body: Record defects that were not fixed, the limits of the work, and the reason. Where the cause of a problem is not yet known, say so. Do not mark the source of a leak, a draught or a movement as resolved unless the evidence shows it. Keep the unresolved item open, with an owner and a follow-up date, so it is not lost when the job is closed.

instruction.heading: Follow-up and proposed work
instruction.body: Schedule follow-up checks where the risk requires them, such as a return visit after a repair near water. Propose any further work as a separate, approved scope, and do not start it because the closeout revealed it. Follow-up work is a source of revenue for this module, and it is priced and approved like any other work. Record the follow-up date and the person responsible.

procedure: Take before and after photographs from the same position, with consent.
Record the measurements, the materials used and the condition at the end of the work.
List defects, limits and unresolved items, and say why each remains open.
Do not mark the source of a problem as resolved without evidence.
Schedule any follow-up check and name the person responsible.
Propose further work for written approval, and do not start it at closeout.

workedExamples.situation: A patch under a window looks finished, but the stain has returned in the same place after the last rain.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the job be closed as resolved?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The recurring stain shows the moisture source is not resolved. Record the before and after evidence, keep the source open, schedule a follow-up check after rain, and propose a source investigation for approval. Do not mark the leak as resolved on appearance alone.

equipmentAndPpe: Camera or phone for photographs, with consent
Measuring tape and a moisture reading tool where trained to use it

commonErrors.error: Closing a job as resolved because the surface looks clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Record evidence of the source being resolved. If there is none, keep it open.

commonErrors.error: Starting further work found during closeout without approval.
commonErrors.prevention: Propose the work and wait for written approval.

commonErrors.error: Taking photographs from different positions so that before and after cannot be compared.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the same marked position for each photograph.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Closeout does not confirm electrical, gas, plumbing, structural or building compliance. For the NSW wiring rule, which excludes equipment at not more than 50 volts AC or 120 volts ripple-free DC, see (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026), and for the NSW plumbing rule see (plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). The other positions are recorded in “Electrical boundaries and referral”, “Water, plumbing and gas boundaries” and “Structural, roof and facade warning signs”.
Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Before and after evidence is taken from the same positions and recorded.
No source is marked resolved without evidence.
Follow-up work is proposed and approved, not started at closeout.
documentationEvidence: Before and after photographs with positions and dates
Closeout record with unresolved items, owners and follow-up dates
Proposed follow-up work with approval status
summary: Record before and after evidence from the same positions.
Keep unresolved items open until the source is shown to be resolved.
Schedule follow-up and propose further work for approval.

knowledgeChecks.question: A patch looks clean, but the stain returns after rain. How should the job be closed?
options: As resolved, because the surface looks clean and the stain has faded from view to the eye today
With the source kept open, a follow-up check scheduled, and an investigation proposed for approval
As resolved once the client pays the final invoice for the patch and the job is closed
With the stain painted over, so the wall looks finished for the client at handover

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are before and after photographs taken from the same position?
options: So that the change can be compared fairly
To make the photographs look more professional
Because the client requires a specific angle

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the closeout record include about the work when it ended?
options: The measurements, the materials used and the condition when the work ended
Only the photographs, with no notes
